video.title: “Stupid Simple” Apps Are Making Millions While You Overthink

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Will Cannon, who built the B2B lead-data SaaS UpLead and the e-signature SaaS Signaturely. Will describes going from a failed mortgage company to selling email lists, then an agency, then UpLead (about $1M ARR in year one, cold email plus SEO). He then explains how he cloned the e-signature category by mining G2 reviews, building a 'stupid simple' product and proving he could get customers before building. The pair also pitch a free vertical CRM monetised through payments and payroll, and both stress selling before building and that 10k a month is a life-changing target.

ideas.name: UpLead (B2B lead data SaaS)
ideas.one_liner: Self-serve subscription platform selling verified B2B contact data, built to replace a manual list-selling agency.
ideas.business_model: Monthly subscription to B2B contact data
ideas.customer: Small and mid-sized businesses and sales teams needing clean lists of ideal prospects
ideas.problem: Sales teams need accurate B2B prospect lists; the incumbents were ZoomInfo and Sales Genie
ideas.offer: A B2B-only lead database where users build their own prospect lists

acquisition_channels.details: First customers came from cold emailing with lists built using their own tool ('eating our own dog food'), with a script and multiple follow-ups.

quote.text: And we got our first customers through cold email.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

ideas.delivery: Software platform with data sourced from industry relationships and kept clean; emails verified cheaply, phones sampled via a Philippines call center. Built by an outsourced dev team found on Upwork.
unit_economics_claims: MRR went 2K, 5K, 8K, 10K in the first months
ideas.startup_cost: not stated (a first MVP attempt on Elance was lost to a scam)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated; reached about 10K MRR within a few months

acquisition.how: SEO and cold email to limited companies can be run by agents; PECR requires care with sole traders

delivery.how: Software delivers data; data quality upkeep and sourcing need occasional human work

support.how: Agents handle most tickets; he hired a human support person early

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK but B2B personal data is regulated by UK GDPR and PECR; data sourcing must be lawful and legitimate interest documented.

quotes.text: I think it was like 2,000 a month, 5,000 a month, 8,000 a month, 10,000 a month. It just started going.
quotes.speaker: Will Cannon

quotes.text: I think within the first year, we were probably doing a million ARR first year.
quotes.speaker: Will Cannon

ideas.name: The Data Supplier (list-selling agency)
ideas.one_liner: Buy industry contact lists cheaply, package by industry and resell the same digital file repeatedly.
ideas.business_model: One-off sales of bulk lists (his side) and per-lead sales (wife's side)
ideas.customer: Businesses wanting prospect lists, from SMBs to some Fortune 500s
ideas.problem: Companies need a clean list of their ideal prospects
ideas.offer: Industry lists such as realtors, dentists and chiropractors, with custom segments and appended data

pricing.notes: Wife ran a separate per-lead business; customers bought from both

acquisition_channels.details: Ranked number one for terms like 'realtor email lists' using borderline gray-hat SEO.

ideas.delivery: Digital file/link; manually merged and appended CSVs; a team built helper software; emails re-verified and phone accuracy sampled by a Philippines call centre (500 of 10,000 hand-dialled).
unit_economics_claims: Business reached 30-50K a month within 2-3 months
Agency profit high six to low seven figures per year
Lists acquired for next to nothing and resold unlimited times
ideas.startup_cost: Next to nothing per list; around $100 for a list

acquisition.how: SEO plus cold email to companies

delivery.how: Manual CSV manipulation could be agent-driven; sourcing is the hard part

uk_applicability.notes: Reselling personal data lists, especially of consumers and sole traders, collides with UK GDPR and PECR; reselling bought lists without a lawful basis is risky.

tactics.name: Mine G2 reviews to pick and position a software clone
steps: Browse G2 categories for fragmented markets with at least one or two billion-dollar players
Read one- and two-star reviews of leaders to find recurring complaints (e.g. too complex)
Build around one angle such as 'stupid simple' rather than price or features
Check you can acquire customers profitably before building

quote.text: I want to make sure and I want it to the best of my ability that I think I have a the ability to acquire customers profitably before I build the business.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Free tools and templates SEO funnel
steps: Build free online tools (e.g. signature creator) and downloadable contract templates
Rank them via SEO
Funnel visitors to a freemium signup
Use a keyword-rich domain

tactics.name: Window-shop business marketplaces for ideas and benchmarks
steps: Browse BizBuySell or BizBen listings
Read due diligence materials without breaching NDAs
Learn margins, acquisition channels and what to copy

quote.text: you can learn so much digging into their due diligence docs.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Pre-sell before building
steps: Run cold email campaigns for the unbuilt product
Throw up a landing page and test Facebook ads
Build only once you get yeses

quote.text: Figure out how to acquire customers first before you go build the thing.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Phone list quality sampling
steps: Randomly sample 500 from a 10,000-record list
Have a call center hand-dial them
Use the disposition report to estimate disconnected and wrong numbers against a threshold

quote.text: Phones, we had a call center in the Philippines, where we take a subset of the list.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Dog-food cold email
steps: Use your own data product to build prospect lists
Cold email with multi-step follow-ups

tactics.name: Retail plus wholesale dual-channel list sales
steps: Sell bulk lists at flat prices
Run a separate per-lead brand
Capture the same buyer on both ends

lessons.lesson: Prove you can acquire customers profitably before building the product.

quote.text: Figure out how to acquire customers first before you go build the thing.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

lessons.lesson: Cloning works best with one clear angle (simplicity) found from competitor reviews.
A strong owned distribution skill, such as SEO or cold email, is the real moat when anything can be copied.
Digital goods with one-time sourcing cost can be resold unlimited times at high margin.
A free product monetised through higher-margin ancillary services is an untapped model as software costs fall.
A target of 10K a month is life-changing and does not require massive scale.

quote.text: to build a business where you're making 10 grand a month, which is life-changing for 99% of people in the world.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Switch to recurring SaaS from agency when the recurring revenue starts to match, and keep the agency running during transition.
Building a mini brand so you are on buyers' shortlists matters for differentiation.

quote.text: And so building a brand is such a key part of how you differentiate.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

lessons.lesson: Bootstrapped growth to scale needs good people and processes; trial and error in hiring is normal.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with plausible but approximate numbers (ranges, 'I want to say', no verification) and a clear step-by-step story; Chris's ideas are hypothetical.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Will owns UpLead and Signaturely and gives away playbooks to build an email list; Chris promotes TK Owners and sponsor Beehiiv.
